To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a model that infers object-centric representations of a visual scene without any annotations and that we show that our method is capable of learning to decompose a visual scene into objects and to generate 2d views of the scene from different viewpoints.

(i) we propose INFERNO a method to learn object-centric representations without supervision; (ii) our method is trained by minimizing a 2D rendering loss between the input scene and the corresponding rendered output; (iii) we empirically demonstrate the interpretability of our learned representations by manipulating them and observing the corresponding effect on the rendered output; (iv) we show that our learned representations are useful in a downstream reasoning task

we propose INFERNO a method to infer 3D object-centric representations of a scene without supervision, and that our method discovers objects in a 2D scene without supervision, learns interpretable object-centric representations, and is able to solve a downstream task in a zero-shot fashion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning object representations in 3D scenes without supervision.
the question of how we can learn to decompose a visual scene into objects without supervision, and how this decomposition can be used for downstream tasks.
developing a method to infer 3D representations of visual scenes from a collection of 2D views.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose INFERNO (INFERNO: INFERNO: InfEring Object-Centric 2D/3D scene Representations without SupervisiON), a method to infer 2D/2D object-centric representations of scenes without supervision.
our method learns to decomposes a scene into multiple structured object-centric representations without any supervision.
INFERNO is a method to infer 3D object-centric representations of scenes without relying on supervision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we learn to infer object-centric 3D representations from a single RGB image without supervision, and that these representations enable downstream tasks.
we learn a 3D scene representation that is interpretable and useful.
we show a way to learn object-centric representations from unlabelled data and that this can be done in a way that the representations can be interpreted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn object-centric representations of scenes without supervision.
3D object-centric representations can be learned without supervision.
3D representations can be learned from 2D data without supervision.
